contributions.anchor: Form A's own printed total, 'Total Contributions: (to line 1 of report):  $ 12,904.63' (p2), which equals the cover's THIS REPORT cell (12,904.63)
contributions.detail: 5 Form A rows sum to 12,904.63 exactly (6,000.00 + 1,500.00 + 2,500.00 + 1,041.02 + 1,863.61), matching the schedule's own printed total and the cover's This-Report column. The cover's Cumulative Total is 99,381.65 and its Last Report column is 86,477.02 (86,477.02 + 12,904.63 = 99,381.65 exactly), so the schedule is PERIOD-scoped behind a cumulative cover and the prior 86,477.02 is never itemized here. No figure was synthesized by differencing covers. IN-KIND CONVENTION: no row on this schedule is labelled in-kind, so monetary-only and monetary-plus-in-kind give the identical 12,904.63 and the side closes under both.

expenditures.anchor: Form B's own printed total, 'Total Expenditures: (to line 2 of report):  16,004.52' (p3), which equals the cover's THIS REPORT cell (16,004.52)
expenditures.detail: 13 Form B rows sum to 16,004.52 exactly, matching the schedule's own printed total and the cover's This-Report column; the cover's Last Report column is 83,377.13 and 83,377.13 + 16,004.52 = 99,381.65 = the printed Cumulative Total, so this side too is period-scoped behind a cumulative cover. No in-kind labels appear, so both in-kind conventions close identically. Note that the cover prints the SAME cumulative figure, 99,381.65, on the contributions line and on the expenditures line; that is arithmetically correct on both lines independently and is what produces the printed 0.00 cumulative ending balance - it is a coincidence of this zeroed-out final account, not a transcription of one figure into two cells.

escalation_note: 900dpi tight --value crops used only as geometry proofs (4) plus one re-crop of p2 row 5 after a first-pass band-index error; no amount on either schedule was in doubt at full-page resolution, and every printed total closed on the first arithmetic pass.

2.measure_note: rowbands.py returned 30 h_rules on this typed sheet, three of which are NOT printed rules: two text baselines inside data row 2 (23.60, 24.22 - the known baseline-registration defect) and a stray at 99.91 at the very foot of the page. Removing those leaves a clean 2.69-2.71 pct constant pitch (16.84, 19.53, 22.24, 24.93, 27.64, ... 87.20). The 2026 form prints NO grey spacer band, so only ONE leading rule is trimmed (the header-row top); rows[0] is the header-row bottom to the first data-row bottom. 25 bands for the 25 printed data rows, of which only rows 1-5 carry entries. PROOF (900dpi --value crops of the stored geometry): row 1 rendered '$ 6,000.00' (recorded 6000.00); row 5, the LAST transcribed row, rendered '$ 1,863.61' (recorded 1863.61). A first-pass proof that mis-indexed row 5 to band [27.64,30.35] rendered '$ 1,041.02' - the row-4 figure - and the band list was re-derived and re-proved before this record was written.

3.measure_note: rowbands.py returned 49 h_rules here; the run from 27.91 to 63.13 alternates at ~1.35 pct - exactly HALF the printed pitch - because each of the 13 filled data rows registers its text baseline as a rule (the known defect), while from 63.13 down (the blank rows, which carry no text) the detector returns the true 2.71 pct pitch unaided. The regular-pitch subsequence was taken (27.91, 30.62, 33.33, ... 87.46) and the 13 dropped values are exactly the 13 filled rows' baselines. Leading trim: the two-line header box ends at 25.19 and this sheet prints ONE wholly blank table row between the header and the first entry, so rows[0] starts at 27.91 (Sunprint Solutions). The Amount column was NOT detected by rowbands (v_rules_pct returned only the two interior rules at 36.90 and 48.15), so its band was hand-measured off the 200dpi render at 77.5-86.5 pct and then PROVED by the crops below rather than asserted. 22 bands, rows 1-13 filled. PROOF: row 1 rendered '$ 3,497.81' (recorded 3497.81); row 13, the LAST transcribed row, rendered '$ 417.50' (recorded 417.50). deskew_deg reported 0.0 on both pages, so no drift correction was needed.

notes: 3-page 2026 per-candidate scan: p1 the typed cover (2026 form variant, 3-line summary), p2 Form A 'Itemized Report of Contributions (money received)', p3 Form B 'Itemized Report of Expenditures (money spent)'. CHECKED AGAINST THE BORN-DIGITAL FAMILY RULE: none of the three pages carries the 'Document generated with Polimorphic.com' footer, so this filing is NOT a Polimorphic e-filing and was vision-read as instructed. The filing schedule box '30 days after withdrawal or Primary Election elimination' IS checked; the candidate signature is present but the DATE BOX IS BLANK (honest gap - index.csv carries no filing date for this key either). REDACTION, and this is a county act, not a filer omission: on p1 the Street Address and City-Zip cells of the candidate block are covered by a solid black box, and on p2 every donor row's street-address portion is likewise blacked out while the city/state/ZIP tail is left legible. Donor city and state are therefore recorded from what survives; nothing was inferred behind a redaction. Dates are the filer's two-digit-year form ('6/19/26') and are kept verbatim. One donor row is the candidate himself (James Ebert, 1,863.61, 7/12/26) - a self-contribution, reported as one ordinary Form A row and not annotated as a loan.
